title: Parity pin cannot detect client-fixture drift despite header claiming it fails when 'EITHER side drifts'
evidence:
//// These tests embed the canonical values and fail when EITHER side drifts: a fixture edit that isn't
//// mirrored in the payloads (or vice versa) breaks the pin.
detail: The test imports only demo/pdf_prebake and gleam stdlib — it never reads client fixtures. A client-fixture edit alone changes nothing these tests compare; only payload drift is caught.
recommended_fix: Soften the header claim, or generate the literals from the client fixtures (shared module/codegen) so fixture-side drift actually breaks the pin.

evidence:
-    // Aoife: co-applicant Daniel's employer income is a second source.
-    "a-aoife" -> [
-      GetIncomeSourcesByApplicationRow(
-        id: "inc-aoife-1",
-        source_type: "employment",
-        amount_cents: 240_000,
-        note: "Daniel Murphy - Helix Systems",
-      ),
-    ]
-    // Marta: employment-permit holder with a side income from tutoring.
-    "a-marta" -> [
detail: The removed entries existed to match client fixture stories; this diff touches no client fixture and the new tests don't pin income sources. If fixtures still show them, PDF and app disagree again.
recommended_fix: Confirm the client fixtures also dropped these sources (in a visible change), and add an income-source parity pin alongside the flags/positives pins.

title: Sara's report contradicts itself: employer reference 'on file' but document list says 'payslips and landlord reference'
evidence: "The employer reference from Kite Software HR is on file and contactable. The landlord reference is outstanding. One of two reference legs is verified; the other is pending.",
detail: The completeness note in the same applicant says 'Two documents on file — payslips and landlord reference', omitting the employer reference the reference note says is on file.
recommended_fix: Make the document list read 'payslips and employer reference' for Sara; same check for Tom, whose listed landlord reference was declined.

title: competition_ranks tie branch is untestable via demo data and untested elsewhere
detail: Demo scores are all distinct, so the tie-sharing path (the port's reason to exist per its docstring) never executes and no test exercises it.
recommended_fix: Add a direct unit test of competition_ranks with tied scores, e.g. [Some(86), Some(86), Some(78)] expecting [Some(1), Some(1), Some(3)].

title: Toast test named 'banner survival' never asserts the consent banner renders
detail: Assertions cover toast-container, message text, one z-index class literal, and absence of the old position class — nothing verifies the banner element survived.
recommended_fix: Assert the banner's own selector/z-index (2147483000) renders in the same HTML, or drop 'banner survival' from the test name.

title: category_scores not covered by the new parity pins and already diverge for Marta (null vs key omitted)
detail: demo_store's a-marta analysis carries \"rental_history\":null\"; the PDF payload omits the key entirely. The new pins cover flags/positives/statements but not category scores.
recommended_fix: Include category_scores in the canonical parity test, normalising null-vs-absent to one convention across demo_store and payloads.

title: Insight-length floor (>1200) sits within roughly one sentence of Liam's brief
detail: Liam's insight — the shortest, four paragraphs — measures ~1200-1250 chars; any prose trim to that applicant's brief trips the build despite acceptable depth.
recommended_fix: Lower the floor to a comfortable margin (e.g. 900) or assert paragraph count instead of raw length.
